### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via WebhookSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via credentialsRef (literal, a string literal in a comment in DeclaredField))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via DERIVED (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via credentialsRef (literal, a string literal in a comment in DeclaredField))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7e2e81c7037d7ed348bd8bea9f2229eabbb474d7` — the merge of head `e86f32235fc03bc032d3b1aaf271e23feaad69b5` into base `3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7e2e81c7037d7ed348bd8bea9f2229eabbb474d7 && git checkout 7e2e81c7037d7ed348bd8bea9f2229eabbb474d7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f e86f32235fc03bc032d3b1aaf271e23feaad69b5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f && git merge --no-ff e86f32235fc03bc032d3b1aaf271e23feaad69b5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e86f32235fc03bc032d3b1aaf271e23feaad69b5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/webhook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/webhook-meta-door-credential-redaction.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/24994-webhook-credential-marker.md, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts (`getMetadataTypeSchema`, `listMetadataTypeSchemaTypes`, `listUnregisteredKindSchemaTypes`, read on main), packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-redaction.ts (`redactorFor`, `hasMetadataRedactor`, `planCarryForward`, read on main), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`carryForwardRedactedCredentials`, read on main), packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-credential-projection.ts (the `flow` precedent's served-form doctrine, read on main), packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts (the fail-closed caution the ruling cites, read on main), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the level-axis rule that reds this head, read on main)

Inputs: card #24994 (body, claim 6304417396, dev reports 6307031456 and 6307426041); #24966 and its ruling record 6304303975; PR #25036 body, file list, and the three-dot diff against `origin/main` at the head; the check-runs on the head. Disclosure (#9387, 5323310017) holds in this record: location, rule and abstract reach only.

Re-review of head `e86f32235fc0` after the FAIL rendered on `0cf6eed565` (one point: the changeset level). The new head is `0cf6eed565` + a merge of `origin/main` (`bae44d37be`) + one commit. The delta on the PR's seven files, read by explicit sha (`git diff 0cf6eed565 e86f32235fc0 -- PR files`), touches ONLY `.changeset/24994-webhook-credential-marker.md`: `patch` becomes `minor`, the headline gains the `spec!:` prefix, and a `**BREAKING:**` banner is added; the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line and the ADR-0087 marker are unchanged. The net three-dot diff against `origin/main` lists the same seven files; the six code and test files are byte-identical to the previous head, so every ① and ③ judgment below is re-adopted unchanged. The PR body's semver line and a "Fix round" section were edited; neither carries a probe, reproduction or served value.

### ① Derived judgments

**The marker (ruling item 1).** `WebhookSchema.secret` carries `.meta({ credential: 'value' })` and `WebhookSchema.headers` carries `.meta({ credential: 'map' })`, on the existing zod `.meta` convention; `headers` is marked as a whole map. No key is added, removed or re-typed; the two fields keep `.optional()` and their descriptions. The marker vocabulary is closed (`value` | `map`) and declared once in `metadata-credential-fields.ts` (`CREDENTIAL_FIELD_KINDS`). Faithful.

**The derivation, once, in the registry (ruling item 2, shape).** `getMetadataTypeRedactor(type)` now resolves `EXTRA_METADATA_TYPE_REDACTORS` → `BUILTIN_METADATA_TYPE_REDACTORS` → `derivedCredentialRedactorFor(getMetadataTypeSchema(type))`. The precedence the ruling binds (explicit, then built-in, then derived) is the literal `??` chain. `datasource` keeps its built-in (pinned: `config.password` still the datasource redactor's answer) and `flow` keeps its plugin registration (pinned generically: an explicit registration wins over a derived one). Neither is migrated. The derivation reads `getMetadataTypeSchema(type)` as ruled (`metadata-type-schemas.ts:299`), which resolves extras → built-ins → `UNREGISTERED_KIND_SCHEMAS`, so `webhook` is reached with no registration call; the unit test pins "zero registration calls" and that an unmarked type derives `undefined` ("serve as is"). `listMetadataTypeRedactorTypes()` includes derived types. Faithful.

**Purity.** `deriveCredentialRedactor` never mutates its input: `withoutKeyAt` copies every container on the path; an item with nothing to withhold is returned by reference with `redactedKeys: []`; `redactedKeys` is sorted and dotted, as the `MetadataRedactionResult` contract requires. No I/O. The walk invokes `lazy` getters and `.meta()` reads, both deterministic. Memoisation is a `WeakMap` on schema identity, so the walk runs once per schema object and a re-registered schema derives afresh. A marker outside the vocabulary fails closed (read as `value`, or `map` on a record) and the ratchet reds on the spelling. Faithful.

**Key question — removal versus substitution (card item 2 against item 5).** The literal text: card item 2 "drops every marked field (not masked) and serves its cleared form (an empty string for a value, an empty map for a map), and names them in `redactedKeys`"; ruling item 2 "every marked field is dropped (not masked) and served as its cleared form"; ruling item 4 "the redaction form (`secret` and the whole `headers` map dropped, cleared forms served)". The dev REMOVES the key from the served item when it holds credential material, names it in `redactedKeys`, and serves a stored cleared form (`''` / `{}`) as written without naming it. The two sentences of item 2 cannot both be read as "substitute": a served `''` is a blank mask, and item 2 says dropped, not masked. Read against item 5 of the card (and item 4 of the ruling), which keeps the write-path carry-forward "accepted and keyed, as today" and requires that "a save that omits the two fields keeps the stored values": `planCarryForward` (metadata-protocol, on main, unchanged by this PR) grafts the stored value only where the incoming value `sameValue`s what the redactor would have served for the row at rest. Under substitution, an incoming `''` would equal the served `''` and be grafted over, so a credential could never be cleared through the save door, and a save that OMITS the key (undefined ≠ `''`) would NOT be grafted and would lose the stored value — the exact opposite of item 5's literal sentence. Under removal, an omitted key equals the served absence and is carried forward (item 5 holds), and `''` is the one door that clears, which is the doctrine the ruling's own cited precedent states in so many words (`flow-credential-projection.ts`: "Dropped, not masked"; "the cleared form is served as written, so a reader can tell cleared from withheld"). **Judgment: removal is WITHIN the ruling** — it is the only reading of item 2 under which item 5 holds with the carry-forward "as today", it matches both existing redactors the ruling names as precedent, and it was disclosed in the PR body, the dev report's deviations list and the changeset. It is not a deviation that needs the maintainer: the maintainer's words took the shape (marker + derivation, 「类似的问题都可以这样处理」); the served-form sentence is the director's wording, and the ruling's item 4 presents the form as "unchanged from B". The B record (6303716122) was outside this review's inputs; the coordinating seat has since read it and reports its item 2 as "dropped, not masked", which closes the one residual the first round left open. Pinned in the diff: drop + `redactedKeys: ['headers', 'secret']`, cleared forms served by reference and unreported, a nested `value` marker inside a wrapper, the stored-row seam in both spellings, and a dogfood round trip of the served form that keeps the stored values in both compositions.

**The ratchet (ruling item 3).** `metadata-credential-fields.test.ts` reads `listMetadataTypeSchemaTypes()` PLUS `listUnregisteredKindSchemaTypes()`. The card names only the first; the dev's first deviation widens it. This is a faithful reading of item 3, not a departure: the ruling's purpose is the fail-closed half for "any metadata type that marks a field", and `webhook` — the one type the card is about — is bound in `UNREGISTERED_KIND_SCHEMAS` and would never be read by the first list alone (`metadata-type-schemas.ts:346–353` says so deliberately). The ratchet reads exactly the set `getMetadataTypeSchema(type)` can resolve, which is the registry the derivation reads (ruling's governing text, :299). It imposes none of the KIND obligations that comment reserves for the registered list; it reads shape only. The credential vocabulary (secret, password, passwd, token, signing, credential, api key; name words or first sentence of the description), the "can hold a credential" limit (string, record, union, unknown; a numeric token budget does not red), and the allow-list (one entry, `datasource:external.credentialsRef`, with a cannot-rot pin) are as ruled: explicit and near-empty. Two further honesty pins (closed vocabulary, `map` only on a record; no marker where the walk cannot reach it, with a probe that the probe itself sees such a marker) are additive and within the spirit of the datasource caution. Synthetic red-then-green case present.

**Door pins.** Both compositions boot (with and without plugin-webhooks, guarded by a composition pin); every door the card names is pinned (meta list in both spellings, item, layered view, published, stored-row data door and its history twin), plus the protocol's `getMetaItems`/`getMetaItem`; admin and member tokens for the meta doors, admin for the data door; each read carries a positive control (200 and the webhook's name) so an empty or refused answer cannot pass; the stored row is pinned unredacted; the dispatcher's declared-webhook source is pinned to still carry both fields with the plugin mounted (delivery signing untouched, item 5). The ablation (marker removed, pins red; restore, pins green) is REPORTED by the dev; this review ran nothing and does not vouch for it. Note (not a defect): `hasMetadataRedactor('webhook')` is now true, so the save door performs the carry-forward's stored-row read for webhook saves — intended by item 5.

### ② Semver level

Changeset at this head: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, a `spec!:` headline and a `**BREAKING:**` banner naming the narrowing (the `/meta` read doors no longer serve a webhook's `secret` or `headers`), `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on both the PR body and the changeset, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` in the repo's exact convention (eleven precedents on main), with the reason stated (no authorable key, export or stored shape removed or renamed). No public export added: the new module is not re-exported from the kernel barrel; `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (which carries `check:api-surface` and `check:generated`) is green on this head.

**Level, judged:** the card and ruling 6304303975 wrote "`@objectstack/spec` patch changeset, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`", and the previous head followed that literally — which `Check Changeset` refused on the level axis ("a declared `narrowing` is a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`", `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, maintainer ruling 2026-09-04, decision batch #35, on #15294). That is the maintainer's standing rule and outranks the director seat's workload line; every `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` changeset on main (eight read) is graded `minor`, and this one now is. The narrowing declaration itself is correct (the doors return less for `webhook`), and `minor` is the right grade for it. No maintainer escalation is owed: the governing ruling already decides it. `Check Changeset` is green on this head (two runs, both success).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviations, answered: (1) ratchet over registered + unregistered-kind schemas — accepted, see ①. (2) removal rather than substitution — accepted as within the ruling, see ①; B's record 6303716122 ("dropped, not masked") confirms it, per the coordinating seat. (3) door set widened by the protocol's two reads, no MCP pin — accepted: the card names no MCP door, and the widening is additive. (4) walker helpers exported from a non-barrel module; `credential` now appears in the generated JSON Schema of `webhook` as an annotation — accepted; the dev reports `check:generated` with all 14 artifacts up to date and no committed artifact changed; CI will confirm. (5) no label written — not this review's concern. (6) worktree removed — not this review's concern.
- Disclosure (#9387): the PR body, the changeset, the dev report and all three test files carry location, rule and abstract reach only. Fixture credentials are self-evidently fake placeholders; every pin asserts absence of a declared key by rule, with the door path as location. Ablation and gate output appear as counts, never as a served value. Held.
- Check-runs on head `e86f32235fc0` at this read (2026-10-21): **no red.** Green: Auto Label, Build Core, Check Changeset (two runs), Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, Test Core (1/6), The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter. In progress: Test Core (2/6) through (6/6). Skipped (opt-in or not applicable): 18.x upgrade harness, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate (sharded), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance, and the duplicate skipped rows of Auto Label and Check PR Size from the second workflow run. The queue guard reads the merge group; the remaining Test Core shards are CI's to finish.
- Previous head `0cf6eed565`: FAIL rendered by this seat on the one point the fix round answers (`Check Changeset`, level axis). Superseded by this record.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` declared NOT MEASURED locally by the dev; it is CI's to decide.
- Out-of-scope finding noted by the dev (a doubly proxied `lazySchema` throws on `_zod` reads) is handled in this PR by reading `.def` first and is pinned; the finding itself carries no carrier and is not filed. Not this review's concern.
